title: Fiscal policy and sovereign debt
sources: IMF World Economic Outlook (WEO) database, via the IMF DataMapper API
IMF Fiscal Monitor, via the IMF DataMapper API
IMF Public Finances in Modern History, via the IMF DataMapper API
IMF Global Debt Database, via the IMF DataMapper API
Kenya National Treasury and its Public Debt Management Office
Fitch Ratings, S&P Global Ratings and Moody's Ratings sovereign rating actions
note: Fiscal policy and sovereign debt for the four markets, built to the same convention as macro.json: one source name, a source_url, an api_url, the indicator code, and a source_last_updated per block, with the period each figure covers. It is a SIBLING file, not an extension of macro.json, because macro.json is scoped to the World Bank inflation and GDP series and its countries array is consumed positionally by the panel; adding fiscal blocks there would either fork that schema or bloat it. macro.json is left byte-identical. Nothing here was estimated, interpolated or carried forward: a figure is either the value the source publishes for that exact year, or a figure quoted verbatim from a fetched source document, and where a source was not reachable the field is absent with the reason recorded in unreachable. GROSS versus NET debt, CENTRAL versus GENERAL government versus the PUBLIC SECTOR, and an ACTUAL versus a PROJECTION are three separate things and each block is labelled for all three.

conventions.gross_vs_net: Gross debt is the debt stock before deducting government deposits and cash balances. Net debt deducts them. Both are carried where the source publishes both, and each block says which it is in its measure field. A gross ratio and a net ratio are never compared as if they were the same figure.
conventions.coverage: General government covers central government plus state, provincial and local government plus social security funds. Central government covers the national government only. Public sector covers the federal or central government plus sub-national governments. Each block states its coverage; the three are different totals and are not substitutes for one another.
conventions.actual_vs_projection: The IMF DataMapper series for the World Economic Outlook and Fiscal Monitor indicators run through 2031. The IMF states that the WEO carries the present plus projections for the current year and the following five years, and the Fiscal Monitor uses the same current-year-plus-five horizon. The current vintage year is 2026, so every value from 2026 onward is a PROJECTION and is flagged projected true point by point, and 2025 and earlier are the historical published years. A projected point is never presented as a reported result.
conventions.local_currency: Debt in local currency is carried only where the source publishes it. No local currency figure was derived from a ratio and no USD figure was converted by this build: where a USD figure appears it is the conversion the source itself published.
